title: ～よりも — “more than ～ / rather than ～”
summary: Gives the standard of comparison: “more than ～.” より marks what is compared against, and も adds emphasis. It follows a noun or a plain-form phrase, and the main clause often has ほう or a comparative idea. Slightly more emphatic than plain より.

patterns.gloss: B is more … than the noun

patterns.form: 動詞・形容詞 普通形＋よりも
疑問詞（何・だれ など）＋よりも

body.p: A よりも B のほうが～ means B is more ～ than A. In 去年よりも今年のほうが忙しい the standard (去年) comes first and the chosen one (今年) takes のほうが.
To compare actions, put the plain form before よりも: 話すよりも、書くほうが伝えやすい. It means “writing is easier than speaking.” The verbs here are in the dictionary form.
何よりも, だれよりも, どこよりも all mean “more than anything / anyone / anywhere else”, i.e. the most. 何よりも健康が大切だ is a common phrase for “health comes first.”

examples.ja: 去年（きょねん）よりも今年（ことし）のほうが忙（いそが）しい。
examples.romaji: Kyonen yorimo kotoshi no hou ga isogashii.
examples.tr: This year is busier than last year.

examples.ja: 話（はな）すよりも、書（か）くほうが自分（じぶん）の考（かんが）えを伝（つた）えやすい。
examples.romaji: Hanasu yorimo, kaku hou ga jibun no kangae o tsutae yasui.
examples.tr: It’s easier to convey my thoughts by writing than by speaking.

examples.ja: 何（なに）よりも、まず健康（けんこう）が大切（たいせつ）だ。
examples.romaji: Nani yorimo, mazu kenkou ga taisetsu da.
examples.tr: More than anything, health comes first.

pitfalls: よりも goes after the thing that loses the comparison, not the winner: 去年よりも今年 (this year is higher).
With a question word, よりも gives a superlative meaning; do not translate it as a plain comparison.
